content:
Added plugins/pmcro-reflector/skills/reflect-and-seed/scripts/Test-QueueRootDerivation.ps1, a self-contained, deterministic regression check (following this repo's existing Test-*.ps1 convention) for the QueueRoot path-derivation bug fixed in trail fdd09c8b-6517-4858-a6d0-be15659aa649. It drives two minimal orchestrate->plan->make->check->reflect-and-seed cycles against disposable scratch trails under the system temp folder -- one with an absolute custom -PmcroRoot, one reproducing the default relative '.\.pmcro' usage -- and asserts the resulting queue item lands under the correct root each time. It accepts -ReflectorScriptPath so it can be pointed at any copy of Complete-ReflectAndSeed.ps1, which let both Maker and, independently, Checker prove it actually catches the regression: run against a freshly-reverted, deliberately-buggy scratch copy, it exited non-zero with a clear per-case failure message, and against the real fixed script it exits 0. It was not enough to write a script that always passes -- Checker re-derived both outcomes from scratch, on its own reverted copy, and got the same results Maker reported.

A genuinely new detail about the original bug surfaced along the way, worth recording since the prior cycle's Reflection didn't know it: the pre-fix QueueRoot line had two distinct failure modes depending on how -PmcroRoot was supplied, not one. An absolute -PmcroRoot (Split-Path down to the drive root, then a hardcoded '.pmcro\queue' literal re-appended) silently wrote the queue item to the wrong, unrelated location -- the failure originally found and fixed. But the literal default relative value ('.\.pmcro', unspecified -PmcroRoot) Split-Paths down to an empty string, which Windows PowerShell 5.1's Join-Path refuses outright with a parameter-binding exception -- a hard crash, not a silent misplacement. This path was apparently never actually exercised in real prior usage (queue items already existed in the repo from before this session, implying earlier callers always passed an explicit, non-default -PmcroRoot, hitting the silent-misplacement mode instead). The already-shipped fix handles both call shapes correctly, and this new regression script now covers both.

Everything planned for this cycle is done and independently verified; nothing about it points to further follow-up work.
